clue.text: The Yorkshire hairpiece? Get it!

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is clipped to t', a single letter
a wig is a hairpiece

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a Yorkshireman's toupee, with an order to fetch it.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously shortens 'the' to t' ('down t' pit'), which supplies the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig something is informal British slang for grasping or understanding it.

clue.text: Simply awful catching cold after 29 competition

indicators.note: after places the round letter first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: the answer to 29 down is a ring, and a ring is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: catching means the jumbled letters hold another letter within them
awful suggests the letters of simply are in a terrible mess, so rearranged

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A sporting event judged dreadful because it spread a cold among competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges SIMPLY to LYMPIS; 'catching' puts C inside it as LYMPICS, which follows O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympic Games are the world's foremost multi-sport contest, so they are a competition.

clue.text: China is ascending here?

parts.note: the continent where China is rising; the letters across the end of China, is and the start of ascending also read upward to give it

explanation.surface: A remark on China's rise as a world power, with a question about where that rise is happening.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upward, 'chinA IS Ascending' hides the answer, but 'ascending' would both signal the upward reading and lend its first letter, so the parse records the clue as one riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the largest nation of the continent named, so the whole clue points to its continent.

clue.text: Secretary in ripped jeans grasps English language

indicators.note: grasps means the assembly takes hold of one more letter, added at its tail
in places the secretary inside the rearranged letters of jeans
ripped jeans are torn apart, so the letters of jeans are rearranged

parts.note: PA is personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: An office secretary in torn denim keeps a grip on the English language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripped jeans' reads as a fashion phrase, but 'ripped' is the anagram signal, giving JANES; 'grasps' then tacks on the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese is the tongue spoken in Japan, a language in its own right.

clue.text: Stopped being quiet to break record

indicators.note: to break the record is to split it open and put something in the gap

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is a record
ease is a state of calm, being quiet and at rest

explanation.surface: An athlete who halted while the crowd hushed, then smashed a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased and stopped are straightforward synonyms in the past tense: both mean came to an end.

clue.text: Liberating, free and paradoxically humorous

indicators.note: free means the letters are let loose to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of liberating comedy: freeing and full of witty paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges LIBERATING. W. S. Gilbert, of Gilbert and Sullivan operetta fame, was known for topsy-turvy paradoxical plots.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbertian describes the absurd, paradoxical humour typical of W. S. Gilbert's comic operas.

clue.text: Special artificial intelligence takes in hill for enlightenment

indicators.note: takes in means the outer letters swallow another piece inside them

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A clever computer program surveys a hilltop and gains wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the Zen Buddhist term for sudden spiritual awakening, a state of enlightenment.

clue.text: Prepare carbon monoxide at absolute zero

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide
absolute zero is 0 K, zero kelvin, read as letters

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab instruction: prepare a gas at the lowest possible temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Cook, a founding backer of Private Eye, fits the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook a meal is to prepare it, so the verbs share a kitchen sense.

clue.text: Healthy society shapes futurist

parts.note: well means in good health

explanation.surface: A thriving society that shapes the future thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wells, Private Eye writer, ties into the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells wrote The Time Machine and The Shape of Things to Come, famous visions of the future.

clue.text: Reading two articles about crime problem over coffee

indicators.note: about means the two articles sit around the rearranged letters

parts.note: A and AN are both indefinite articles

indicators.note: a problem with the word crime turns its letters into a new order

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone reading articles about a crime problem over a morning coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' is just scene-setting. The two articles are A and AN, wrapped 'about' MERIC, which 'problem' makes from the letters given.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a common style of coffee.

clue.text: Radiation in school's not right, doctors say

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out one letter

parts.note: a grammar school is a type of British state secondary school; the 's is just 'is' as a link

indicators.note: doctors as a verb means tampers with, so the letters of say are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doctors warn that radiation in a school isn't safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one R from GRAMMAR (a selective British state school) to get GAMMAR; 'doctors' rearranges SAY to AYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma rays are a form of high-energy electromagnetic radiation emitted by radioactive decay.

clue.text: Bear or blackbird?

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
a rook is a crow-family bird

explanation.surface: A wildlife riddle: is that a bear or a blackbird?
explanation.walkthrough: 'blackbird' splits into black and bird. Danae Brooke wrote for Private Eye, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate it, as in 'brook no argument', the verb sense of bear.

clue.text: Secret soldier

definitions.meaning: the lowest rank in the army

explanation.surface: An undercover soldier on a covert mission.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye, the satirical magazine, is the puzzle's theme, celebrating its 1500th issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Private means confidential, and a private is the rank of an ordinary soldier.

clue.text: Fruit bat home? Not in, definitely out

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: home means 'at home', i.e. in; not in says to drop the at from the next word

parts.note: taken as the word itself before removal
'at home' means in, so home points to the word at that is to be removed

explanation.surface: A fruit bat checking its roost, finding nobody in and going out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' means in, so 'home? Not in' strips AT from BAT, leaving B. In cricket an lbw decision that is plumb is beyond doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket commentators call a batsman plumb lbw when the dismissal is unarguable, certainly given out.

clue.text: A trap to steal pound loses penny? That's surprising

indicators.note: to steal is to take something in, so the trap holds the shortened pound

parts.note: a sting is a police trap or confidence trick

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped

parts.note: the word pound before trimming

explanation.surface: A con trick to steal money that ends up a penny short: what a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: A sting is a confidence trick or police trap; 'loses' leaves OUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding and surprising are synonyms: both describe something that greatly amazes.

clue.text: Dear, dear! Tablet dropped by Heather

indicators.note: dropped tells us a letter is let fall from the word

parts.note: the word dear taken at face value
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay as a pill is dropped by a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Darling and dear are both endearments used for a loved one.

clue.text: Dwarf, for example, acquires second name after retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
acquires means the outer piece takes the others inside

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A dwarf who takes a second name once he retires.
explanation.walkthrough: EG takes in MON as EMONG; 'after retiring' reverses it. Lord Gnome is Private Eye's fictional proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a small mythical being, like a dwarf, often pictured as a garden ornament.

clue.text: Angry over spill

definitions.meaning: to knock over and spill something

explanation.surface: Someone cross about a spilled drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset means distressed, overturned, and to knock over, so it fits all three readings.

clue.text: Look both ways

definitions.note: to look at something closely is to watch it, the same word read either way

indicators.note: both ways says the word reads the same from left or right

parts.note: to look at something closely is to watch it, the same word read either way

explanation.surface: Road-safety advice: look left and right before crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or regard it closely, a verb sense of look.

clue.text: Old girlfriend inclined to be stretched

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
tended means leaned towards, was inclined

explanation.surface: A former girlfriend inclined to be strung out.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended means lengthened or drawn out, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Prelude to main trombone part

indicators.note: part means only a piece of the words main trombone is taken

explanation.surface: A trombone's opening passage before the main theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening section that serves as a prelude.

clue.text: Follow progress of time by lines

parts.note: to track is to follow the progress of something
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Tracking how time passes through lines on a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Trackage is the total length of railway track, so a network's lines.

clue.text: Water plant or shrub vigorously about mid-July

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the inner pair
shaken vigorously, the letters of shrub are rearranged
mid takes the middle letters of the month's name

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: water a plant or shrub well around mid-July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' seems a verb in the surface but belongs to the definition. 'vigorously' makes BRUSH, which goes 'about' the centre pair of 'mid-July'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulrush is a tall reed growing at the water's edge, an aquatic plant.

clue.text: Scottish nobles retreat down south

parts.note: a lair is a hiding place or retreat

explanation.surface: Highland aristocrats retreating southwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Laird is the Scots word for a landowner of an estate, so a member of the landed gentry.

clue.text: Kind of piece, decorated with colour

indicators.note: decorated with means the inner piece is covered by the outer one

parts.note: a hue is a colour
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Describing a type of artwork decorated in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'type of'; 'Kind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate and merciful, the adjective sense of kind.

clue.text: Weight of silver in 1,000kg

indicators.note: in places the metal symbol inside the unit

parts.note: a metric tonne is 1,000 kilograms
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: How much silver is in a tonne.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is a measure of weight or carrying capacity, especially of ships.

clue.text: Cooked food really is excellent, deserves tips

indicators.note: tips are the front ends of the words, so the opening letter of each is taken

explanation.surface: A diner says the cooked food is so excellent it deserves a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like restaurant gratuities, but it means the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried describes food cooked in hot fat, a particular way of cooking.

clue.text: Limit of returned books

indicators.note: returned means the word of is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A library's cap on how many books may be brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Foot, Private Eye journalist, fits the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot of a page or bed is its lower end, its limit.

clue.text: Might they reserve fellow's prize?

parts.note: one who books (reserves) a man might whimsically be called a ...; the real name is a literary prize

explanation.surface: A question of whether some people set aside a man's award.
explanation.walkthrough: The Man Booker was the sponsored name of the Booker Prize for fiction; Christopher Booker co-founded Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The Man Booker Prize was the UK's best-known award for a novel, so it is a prize.

clue.text: By wearing glasses, start to notice county briefly

indicators.note: wearing means the multiplication sign is inside the glasses

parts.note: a pair of spectacles looks like two Os
x means by, as in 3 x 4 dimensions

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of notice

explanation.surface: A tourist putting on spectacles to take in a short tour of a county.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxon is the standard abbreviation for Oxfordshire, an English county, so a county shortened.

clue.text: Call round

explanation.surface: An invitation to telephone or come over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring means both to telephone and a circular band, covering each sense.

clue.text: Tory disrobed in and around church ceremony

indicators.note: disrobed strips off the outer layer, the end letters of the word
around tells us the letters of in and are turned about into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Tory politician undressing in and around a church: a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a Conservative; 'disrobed' strips its ends, and 'around' turns IN AND into DINAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is a prescribed religious rite, such as communion, a church ceremony.

clue.text: Newspaper roaming all over the place? I'm lost

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters of roaming are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; lost signals these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A newspaper delivery person wandering about confused, admitting to being lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I'M from ROAMING and rearrange; 'lost' signals the removal. Private Eye is the organ in this themed puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a publication representing a group's views, such as a party newspaper.
